draft.text:
Own the production object-detection model running on Northcairn Robotics' warehouse robot fleet end to end, from data collection through deployment (Mar 2021 - present).
Led the migration of the perception stack from a two-stage to a single-stage detector in PyTorch, cutting inference time on the robot's onboard hardware.
Set research direction for the perception team jointly with the team lead, and drove the architecture decision behind the detector migration.
Mentor two junior applied scientists on the perception team informally (no budget or hiring authority attached to the role); previously trained two new hires at Fenwick Vision Systems on the team's model evaluation process.
Gatekeep quality for each quarterly firmware update by reviewing model-release sign-off documents before release.
Authored the model card and evaluation report at Fenwick Vision Systems that the QA team used to sign off on every model release.
Provided on-call support for the perception service during fleet pilot deployments at Northcairn.
Diagnosed a production accuracy regression at Fenwick, tracing it to a change in the camera lighting rig, and co-authored an internal technical report on perception failure modes that the hardware team used to prioritise camera placement changes.
Reduced false-positive detections on reflective packaging by retraining the model with a targeted hard-negative dataset.
Filed a patent with two co-inventors on detecting reflective surfaces in warehouse aisles.
Contributed to the perception team's active-learning pipeline for label prioritisation and presented the results at the company's internal research seminar.
Built the first version of the label-review tool used by external data annotation contractors, and the labelling tool used by Fenwick's QA team.
Built and maintained the quarterly retraining pipeline for Fenwick's defect-detection model, and deployed that model to factory-floor inspection stations.
Ported inference code from a GPU server to a lower-power embedded board for a pilot deployment; production model code across roles has been Python and C++.
Worked across team boundaries at Aldermoor Institute on a joint project with the robotics group on real-time inference under compute constraints, and built the lab's shared dataset-loading library adopted by three other research projects.
Published two peer-reviewed workshop papers on convolutional feature extraction for small-object detection and presented a poster to a workshop audience of roughly forty attendees.
Wrote the lab's internal guide to reproducible experiment tracking at Aldermoor Institute.
Hands-on engineer throughout: 10+ years building, deploying and supporting computer-vision systems on on-premise robot and factory hardware; have not yet held a formal people-management role with hiring or budget ownership.

job.raw_text:
Engineering Manager, Platform Team
Nimbus Cloudworks - Hybrid (Berlin) or Remote (EU)

Who we are

Nimbus Cloudworks makes the internal developer platform that other companies build
their own platforms on top of. Our Platform team is the backbone of the engineering
org: deployment tooling, on-call standards, and the infrastructure everyone else
depends on to ship.

The role

We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead our Platform team through its next phase
of growth. You'll manage a small group of backend engineers, own the team's roadmap
and budget, and be the person who represents platform concerns when the rest of the
company is planning. We want someone who has been a hands-on engineer before and
still remembers what that's like.

What you'll own

- Directly managing a team of software engineers: hiring, growth, and performance
- The team's budget for cloud infrastructure spend
- Running incident response and postmortems when platform services go down
- Representing the team in quarterly cross-org planning
- Setting the team's technical roadmap in partnership with senior engineers

What we're looking for

- 3+ years directly managing a team of software engineers, including hiring and
  performance reviews
- Experience owning a team budget, not just contributing estimates to one
- A background as a hands-on software engineer before moving into management
- Experience running incident response and postmortems for production outages
- Comfortable representing the team in cross-org planning conversations
- Genuinely good at giving feedback that people can act on

Nice to have

- Experience in a regulated industry such as payments or healthcare
- Familiarity with Kubernetes or a comparable orchestration platform
- Experience scaling a team from a handful of engineers to a larger one
- Public speaking or conference experience
- Experience setting a company-wide technical strategy, not just a team one

What we offer

Competitive compensation, a relocation package if you need one, generous parental
leave, and a team that has been through an incident or two together. Nimbus
Cloudworks is committed to building a diverse and inclusive team.
